transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-19
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Jasmine Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Morris (Redwood SE), Sofia Alvarez (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Head of ML - Hightide), Marcus Chen (Eng Manager), Priya Kapoor (Data Privacy), Omar Lee (Product), Samir Rao (SRE)

Auto Summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
- Initial qualification: Hightide building consumer-facing assistants, needs low-latency for chat, long context (32k-64k) for user history, multilingual (EN/ES/FR), and tool-calling to integrate product APIs.
- Discussed open models, quantization options, and Redwood hosting modes.
- Security and data residency are big constraints (EU and US separation).
- Agreed next steps: share pricing/SOW, upload sample prompts, schedule technical deep dive.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jasmine Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, we can start — I'm Jasmine, AE at Redwood, with Ethan and Sofia from SE.
[00:18] Lena Ortiz: Hi, Lena here — thanks, excited to dig in.
[00:22] Marcus Chen: Marcus from eng, hello.
[00:25] Priya Kapoor: Priya — data privacy.
[00:28] Omar Lee: Omar product. Samir on infra joins in a minute.
[00:32] Jasmine Patel: Great. The objective today is to understand Hightide's model needs — open model choices, context length, multilingual, and tool-calling — so we can recommend hosted vs dedicated vs private. Quick yes on agenda?
[00:45] Lena Ortiz: Yes. Also want to cover SSO and KMS questions, that's a gating item.
[00:49] Jasmine Patel: Noted. Ethan — quick 30-second background on Redwood's options?
[00:54] Ethan Morris: Yeah, sure. We have Redwood Hosted — easiest to get started, pay-as-you-go. Redwood Dedicated is reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and lower unit cost. And Redwood Private gives you a VPC/private control plane or on-prem for strict regs. All share the same API and tool-calling surface, so you can prototype hosted then move to dedicated/private.
[01:20] Marcus Chen: When you say same API — like no code changes for model swap?
[01:23] Sofia Alvarez: Mostly yes, you can pin model versions and swap policies at the routing layer. There are some infra config differences for VPC networking and auth, but your application calls the same endpoints.
[01:36] Lena Ortiz: Good. Our high-level constraints: low-latency for chat threads — average 200ms target for 1-2 token streaming? (laughs) but realistic is more like sub-400ms; cost cap per 1k messages, and very long context — we need user history + session transcripts, so 32k likely minimum, 64k aspirational. Also Spanish and French support, and ability to call our internal product APIs (tool-calling).
[02:05] Ethan Morris: Great, that's helpful. Quick clarifying q: what's your expected qps and peak concurrency?
[02:11] Marcus Chen: For launch phase, 25 qps with bursts to 75, target 99th percentile latency under 600ms for typical prompts.
[02:20] Ethan Morris: Okay, that maps well to Dedicated if you want predictable SLOs, but hosted can work for early stage. A couple tradeoffs: hosted has flexible autoscaling, but you might see more variance in p99 latency; dedicated reduces variance and gives reserved throughput.
[02:36] Omar Lee: Cost-wise, what's the rough delta between hosted and dedicated? ballpark numbers fine.
[02:41] Jasmine Patel: We'll share formal pricing, but redwood dedicated tends to be more cost-efficient at sustained loads because of reserved capacity and optimized batching. Hosted is higher per-token but less commitment. We'll send a page with modeled TCO.
[02:56] Priya Kapoor: On data retention — we cannot have customer PII leave our control in some EU flows. Do you support encrypt-at-rest with customer KMS and tenant-segregated logs?
[03:08] Sofia Alvarez: Yes — Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and VPC, and Dedicated can be configured with private networking and audit logs. Hosted offers encryption and SOC2 controls but not customer-managed KMS unless part of enterprise add-on. We'll include the exact capabilities in the security packet.
[03:27] Samir Rao (joined): Sorry for the delay — Samir here.
[03:29] Samir Rao: Confirming region: we need EU-region hosting for EU-users and US for US. Can Redwood route by policy?
[03:34] Ethan Morris: Yes, smart routing can steer requests by region, tier, or latency. You can have region-specific deployments and routing policies.
[03:41] Lena Ortiz: Let's talk models — open models we evaluated internally: Mistral variants, Llama2/3 forks, MPT-30B, and some 8-bit quantized distilled models. We want to understand accuracy vs latency for 32k and 64k contexts. Also multilingual quality — we care about Spanish legalese.
[04:05] Ethan Morris: Understood. Our model catalog includes curated open models and verified performance profiles. For long context, kernel selection and KV cache matter a lot. For 32k you often keep full KV cache in memory, beyond that you need smart eviction or suffix-only caching to control memory.
[04:25] Marcus Chen: Can you support 128k? we've had internal asks for very long threads — not a must for launch but curious.
[04:31] Sofia Alvarez: Technical answer: it's possible but comes with tradeoffs — throughput and latency degrade as sequence length increases, and some models need specialized compilation paths or chunked tool-calling. For 128k we typically recommend a hybrid approach: summarize older context or store embeddings and retrieve relevant snippets.
[04:49] Lena Ortiz: Summarization is fine, but we want the raw option for certain high-value sessions.
[04:54] Ethan Morris: Totally — Dedicated or Private gives you more headroom for memory and custom kernel flags, so raw long-context sessions are more feasible there.
[05:02] Omar Lee: Tool-calling — we need the model to call our commerce API and a payment verification microservice. How is function calling supported?
[05:10] Sofia Alvarez: We support structured tool calling and function schemas. You can register tools and specify safe execution policies — the model returns structured JSON which your runtime can validate and execute. We'll talk about sandboxing, and we can show an example schem — I mean schema — later.
[05:27] Marcus Chen: Any risk of hallucination when invoking a tool? e.g., false call to payment endpoint.
[05:33] Ethan Morris: This is an active area; we add guardrails: strict schema validation, allow-listing endpoints, and optional verification layers. Additionally the runtime can be configured to require signed tokens for certain calls and we support explicit confirmation prompts before execution.
[05:50] Priya Kapoor: From a compliance view we need detailed audit logs of tool calls and the model inputs/outputs for a 7-year retention window for some EU clients — is that practical?
[05:59] Sofia Alvarez: Audit logs are supported; retention windows can be configured depending on plan and storage. For Private you control retention; for Hosted we offer enterprise add-ons for extended retention. We'll include details.
[06:11] Lena Ortiz: Let's talk evaluation — we want Redwood to run benchmarks on our 200 sample prompts and compare: quality (our rubric), latency, cost per 1k prompt, and model behaviour on Spanish legal text.
[06:24] Jasmine Patel: Great. If you share prompts we'll run a benchmark on hosted and a Dedicated-simulated run to show differences. We'll provide a spreadsheet with results and a short writeup.
[06:36] Lena Ortiz: When you say Dedicated-simulated run — does that mean you don't spin up actual reserved infra?
[06:41] Ethan Morris: For initial benchmarking we typically run on equivalent hardware with controlled scaling to approximate Dedicated performance; if you want, we can schedule a true dedicated pilot but that requires provisioning.
[06:50] Marcus Chen: Pilot sounds good to validate p99 latency. How long to provision?
[06:54] Jasmine Patel: Depends on capacity — usually 2–4 weeks for Dedicated reservation in a specific region. We can fast-track with a trial credit in some cases.
[07:03] Omar Lee: About cost modeling: do you expose per-model token pricing we can pull into our pricing engine?
[07:07] Jasmine Patel: Yes, per-model/unit costs are available and we'll share a CSV. Also Redwood Optimize can give heuristic recommendations for batching and quantization to hit cost targets.
[07:20] Priya Kapoor: For encryption keys — KMS integration options: do you support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and customer HSM?
[07:29] Sofia Alvarez: AWS KMS and GCP KMS supported for Dedicated/Private. For on-prem or strict HSM requirements, Private with HSM integration is available under enterprise plans. Hosted supports provider-managed keys and envelope encryption; customer-managed keys are an enterprise add-on.
[07:44] Samir Rao: Quick question on multiregion: how does data residency work if we route EU users to EU region but need to call a payment API in the US? won't that cross borders?
[07:54] Ethan Morris: Good catch. You can configure routing and tool endpoints; for cross-border calls you'd need to either proxy through EU-hosted gateway or have a regional instance of the payment API. We'll help map architecture options.
[08:08] Lena Ortiz: Let's get into model specifics — for Spanish legal, which open models show strongest performance in your evals?
[08:14] Ethan Morris: From our internal tests Mistral-large variants and a few multilingual Llama3 forks scored best on legal Spanish benchmarks, but they vary a lot by fine-tuning. Also some larger encoder-decoder models can be strong if you fine-tune with domain data. We'll share per-model eval sheets.
[08:33] Marcus Chen: Is there a recommended approach: smaller faster model with retrieval vs bigger model with native long context?
[08:38] Sofia Alvarez: Both valid. Retrieval-augmented pipelines (embedding store + reranker) can give smaller models similar accuracy at lower cost for many queries. For tasks needing full-joint reasoning across long unstructured text, larger models with native long-context tend to be better.
[08:55] Omar Lee: How about model quantization? We want CPU fallback for low-cost cold paths.
[09:01] Ethan Morris: We support quantized variants optimized for inference — int8/4 and mixture-of-precision options. CPU fallback is possible but you'll see latency increases; quantized GPU inference can be a good balance.
[09:12] Lena Ortiz: Any gotchas with tool-calling and quantized models?
[09:16] Sofia Alvarez: Mostly around deterministic structured outputs. Quantization can sometimes alter generation probabilities slightly, which may affect schema adherence; we add validation layers and sometimes use a higher-precision path for tool-calling endpoints.
[09:31] Marcus Chen: Security — SSO and RBAC. We use SAML SSO and need role separation between product and infra teams.
[09:37] Jasmine Patel: Redwood supports SAML/SSO, RBAC with custom roles, and audit trails. We'll provide docs and an onboarding checklist.
[09:46] Priya Kapoor: Does Redwood support IP allow-lists and VPC peering for Dedicated?
[09:51] Sofia Alvarez: Yes to both. Dedicated and Private give more networking control. Hosted has IP allow-listing for API usage but not VPC peering unless in Private/VPC mode.
[09:59] Omar Lee: About SLAs — what does Dedicated SLA look like?
[10:03] Jasmine Patel: Dedicated has uptime and latency targets in the SLA. We'll share the SLA PDF in the follow-ups.
[10:10] (crosstalk)
[10:12] Lena Ortiz: Timeline — we want to launch a v1 in Q4 2025. Is that realistic with a Dedicated or Private path?
[10:19] Jasmine Patel: Yes, Q4 is reasonable. If you start with Hosted and iterate, then transition to Dedicated for scale, that's the fastest path. If compliance blocks hosted for critical flows, start Private early — that'll take longer for provisioning.
[10:33] Marcus Chen: For the evaluation, can Redwood run a side-by-side: Mistral, Llama3-fork, and a quantized 30B model for our prompts?
[10:40] Ethan Morris: Absolutely — we'll run those comparisons and include latency and cost columns. Please share the prompt set and rubric.
[10:47] Lena Ortiz: We'll redact any PII in uploads.
[10:49] Priya Kapoor: We'll need an NDA addendum for certain data sets before sending.
[10:53] Jasmine Patel: We can do that — we have a data handling addendum. I'll attach in follow-up.
[10:58] Samir Rao: On observability — what telemetry do you expose? token-level cost, per-model p50/p95/p99 latencies, per-route dashboards?
[11:07] Sofia Alvarez: Yes, Redwood Console provides token-level cost breakdowns, per-model and per-route latency histograms, tracing hooks, and error analysis. You can connect logs to your SIEM.
[11:18] Marcus Chen: Can we export traces to Jaeger or Datadog?
[11:21] Ethan Morris: We have integrations for Datadog, and you can export traces to external systems via our tracing hooks. We'll include integration docs.
[11:30] Omar Lee: I want to discuss fallback behavior — if a preferred model is busy, can requests fall back to a cheaper variant automatically?
[11:36] Sofia Alvarez: Yes, routing policies support fallbacks — by latency, cost, or availability. For critical user flows you can set automatic fallback to a predefined model variant.
[11:46] Lena Ortiz: Let's role-play a sample flow: a user requests invoice history in Spanish, model should consult retrieval, and then call our payment API for verification. We need high confidence before API calls.
[11:59] Ethan Morris: Implementation: retrieval -> model reasoning -> structured tool output -> validation layer -> signed request to payment API. You can require manual confirm step for >$threshold operations.
[12:12] Marcus Chen: Good. For the retrieval component: do you recommend local vector DB or hosted vector store?
[12:17] Sofia Alvarez: Both. For privacy and residency, local vector DB under your VPC is recommended; hosted vector stores make prototype faster.
[12:26] Lena Ortiz: Anything about model fine-tuning vs retrieval we should know for legal text?
[12:30] Ethan Morris: Fine-tuning on domain data helps a lot for legalese. If you can't fine-tune, retrieval plus prompt engineering and reranking is often the next-best option. We'll include guidance.
[12:40] Priya Kapoor: For fine-tuning data, what's Redwood's policy? Do we retain datasets?
[12:44] Sofia Alvarez: For Hosted fine-tuning we treat data per our data retention policy; enterprise customers can request private fine-tuning workflows where data never leaves their VPC. We'll document options.
[12:55] Omar Lee: Could we do a short pilot: 2-week benchmark with our 200 prompts and 3 models? What would that entail?
[13:03] Jasmine Patel: Pilot outline: 1) NDA/data addendum, 2) Hightide shares prompts + rubric, 3) Redwood runs benchmarks on hosted and simulated dedicated, 4) deliver spreadsheet + writeup, 5) optional Dedicated trial if results look good.
[13:20] Marcus Chen: Sounds good. Cost for pilot?
[13:23] Jasmine Patel: We'll absorb some costs via trial credits; we can outline any excess compute costs.
[13:29] Samir Rao: Network constraints: we prefer no egress to non-approved cloud accounts — can you guarantee that?
[13:36] Ethan Morris: For Private and Dedicated with VPC peering we can restrict egress. Hosted is constrained but we can do allow-lists and IP controls. We'll detail tradeoffs.
[13:48] Lena Ortiz: A few friction points: 1) legal wants written guarantees about EU data staying in EU for certain features, 2) infra wants dedicated p99 SLOs, 3) product wants multilingual parity. Those are our success criteria.
[14:03] Jasmine Patel: Clear. We'll map each criterion to product capabilities in the follow-up.
[14:08] (15:00-minute segment skipped slightly as attendees check internal docs)
[14:12] Marcus Chen: On model lifecycle — how do you handle rollouts and version pins?
[14:16] Sofia Alvarez: You can pin model versions per route, do canary rollouts, A/B tests, and automatic fallback policies. Console shows per-version metrics so rollbacks are easy.
[14:27] Omar Lee: Any known model regressions when moving from hosted to dedicated?
[14:30] Ethan Morris: Regressions are rare if the same model binary is used. Differences arise when quantization or compilation flags change — we recommend regression tests as part of rollout. Redwood Optimize has eval tooling for that.
[14:45] Lena Ortiz: Let's touch on token accounting — we need to know cost per-turn for 32k vs 64k.
[14:51] Jasmine Patel: Cost scales linearly with input length in many models, though batching/kv cache can change per-token effective cost. We'll model scenarios in the pricing sheet.
[15:02] Priya Kapoor: For audit: do you support immutable logs exports?
[15:06] Sofia Alvarez: Yes, we can export logs to S3 or your log store with immutability controls for Private/Dedicated. For Hosted we'll provide enterprise add-ons.
[15:20] Marcus Chen: Implementation detail: can we pin certain sensitive routes to Private while keeping others on Hosted?
[15:25] Ethan Morris: Yes, routing policies can split by route, user, or org. Hybrid deployments are supported.
[15:33] Omar Lee: Regarding multilingual fine-tune: do you help with the fine-tuning pipeline?
[15:37] Sofia Alvarez: We have an expert services team to help with data prep, fine-tuning, and eval. That would be part of professional services.
[15:47] Lena Ortiz: Ok, let's loop back to next steps and owners.
[15:50] Jasmine Patel: Recap: Redwood to share hosted vs dedicated pricing, SOW, security docs and SLA. Hightide to share prompts and compliance questions. We'll schedule the technical deep dive for infra next week. Anything missing?
[16:05] Marcus Chen: Please include a sample rollout plan for moving from hosted to dedicated — timelines and downtimes.
[16:11] Jasmine Patel: Will do.
[16:13] Priya Kapoor: Please include the data handling addendum and any references to KMS/HSM specifics.
[16:18] Jasmine Patel: Noted.
[16:20] Omar Lee: For the pilot, can you include a column for "resiliency risk" in the spreadsheet? e.g., how likely is a fallback to cause function mis-exec?
[16:28] Ethan Morris: Yes, we'll add a simple risk score per model/test.
[16:33] (longer technical aside about KV cache tuning, some folks muted)
[17:05] Ethan Morris: Quick note: for extremely long contexts we may use windowed attention kernels, and some models benefit from sequence parallelism; we'll supply a short tech note explaining options.
[17:18] Samir Rao: How are secrets handled for tool-calls — do you store service tokens?
[17:22] Sofia Alvarez: We recommend tokens be stored in your vault and provided at call-time via short-lived tokens. Redwood can integrate with secret managers for private deploys.
[17:31] Marcus Chen: Anything else on cost optimisation?
[17:34] Jasmine Patel: Redwood Optimize will suggest batching settings, quantization levels, and model switches based on workload. We'll include examples for your traffic profile.
[17:43] Lena Ortiz: I have one more: for Spanish legal we will likely want a small fine-tune. What's the turnaround?
[17:49] Sofia Alvarez: With clean curated data, fine-tuning a 7–13B-ish model can be weeks; 30B+ will be longer and more costly. We'll propose options.
[17:58] Omar Lee: Any regulatory constraints around model provenance? legal wants to know if model weights were derived from proprietary corpora.
[18:05] Ethan Morris: We document model provenance and training data disclaimers when available for open models; for custom fine-tunes you control the data. We'll surface provenance notes in the catalog.
[18:16] (short pause)
[18:22] Jasmine Patel: Ok, time check — we have about 28 minutes left and a tech deep dive to schedule. Should we schedule the infra deep dive now?
[18:29] Samir Rao: Week of 2025-06-30 looks good, prefer Tue/Thu mornings EU friendly.
[18:34] Jasmine Patel: I'll propose slots in the follow-up.
[18:38] Lena Ortiz: Quick question — do you have an example of function schema enforcement you can share?
[18:43] Sofia Alvarez: Yes, we'll attach a short demo JSON schema and an example call.
[18:48] Marcus Chen: Regarding regressions: will Redwood run an automated smoke test on deploy?
[18:52] Ethan Morris: We can run smoke tests and regression evals as part of rollouts — included in the enterprise pattern.
[19:00] Priya Kapoor: One more compliance-related: How do you handle data subject requests (DSRs) under GDPR?
[19:06] Sofia Alvarez: For Private, you have control and can implement DSR workflows. For Hosted, we provide tools and support to process DSRs and can assist operationally via enterprise support. We'll provide the DSR playbook.
[19:18] Omar Lee: Ok, seems we're aligned. Any blockers?
[19:21] Lena Ortiz: Legal needs the addendum, infra wants the dedicated SLOs documented. Those are blockers for procurement.
[19:29] Jasmine Patel: We'll prioritize those in the follow-up packet.
[19:33] (silence as notes are taken)
[19:40] Jasmine Patel: Quick run through of owners: I'll send the pricing and legal docs; Ethan will run the model benchmark outline and latency sketch; Sofia will attach schema examples and security notes. Hightide — Lena will share prompts and Priya will share compliance questions. Samir will confirm region. Anything to add?
[19:58] Marcus Chen: No.
[20:00] Omar Lee: Thanks all.
[20:02] Jasmine Patel: Great — we'll follow up by Tuesday with the packet and proposed times. Thanks everyone.

End of transcript (46 minutes).
